best_idea: Batch every range ring of one colour into one shared vertex buffer with a (start, count) run per colour, so draw cost is two calls per colour, rebuild only when the rings change, and cap frame time with a wait computed from the previous frame end, dropping the cap when the window loses focus.
decision_why: The ring batching shape and the focus-based cap transfer; the donor rebuilds on turn change with static buffers, and Frankendom aggro and leash rings move every tick, so the rebuild trigger and buffer usage must change. Rings are client presentation of engine state and stay out of the engine.
acceptance: A unit test asserts that N rings in C colour groups give 2 x C draw calls (not 2 x N), and that the focused 60 fps and background 15 fps caps give frame waits of exactly 1000/cap ms; on a 375 px phone with 30 aggro rings on screen the play frame holds the focused cap.
